constraint: Keep default 64 visits and the same model/inference batch capacity. User explicitly requires current response speed.
hypothesis: The collector can repeatedly select an already pending child and return an underfilled batch. Exclude pending/exhausted branches to fill available batches, then test reservation counts without a fictitious -1 value.
selection: Highest completed development score; tie prefers original virtual-loss values. No parameter sweep. Freeze winner before fresh evaluation.
strengthGate: At least 108/192, each board at least 12/32, paired bootstrap lower 95% bound >0.5, no illegal/capped games.
speedGate: Fixed 18 roots with unchanged 64 visits on both CPU/WASM and WebGPU; aggregate P95 <= 1.05 baseline and every board P95 <= 1.10 baseline. Record neural batch counts. No increase to default visits or model size.

amendments.stage: After observing first-candidate development results, before inspecting second-candidate results and before any held-out evaluation
amendments.reason: Development already shows a large sphere/torus difference. Use conservative board-specific deployment rather than forcing one reservation rule onto all six boards.
amendments.selection: For each board choose the higher development score from the two candidates only if >=5/8. Otherwise retain the baseline exactly on that board. Candidate ties prefer original virtual-loss values. Freeze the full six-board schedule before any held-out evaluation. Strength and speed gates remain unchanged.
